title: CTS Administration & Leadership — Unit 5: Financial Stewardship and Budgeting

blocks.en: 📖 Administration & Leadership — Unit 5: Financial Stewardship and Budgeting
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Administración y Liderazgo — Unidad 5: Mayordomía financiera y presupuesto

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "He who is faithful in what is least is faithful also in much." — Luke 16:10 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "El que es fiel en lo muy poco, también en lo más es fiel." — Lucas 16:10 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — The Subject Jesus Did Not Avoid
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — El tema que Jesús no evitó

blocks.en: There is an old myth that money is somehow beneath the spiritual leader — that a true man of God should not dirty his hands with budgets and bank accounts. But you cannot read the Gospels honestly and believe that myth. Our Lord spoke about money constantly — more than He spoke of heaven, more than He spoke of prayer. He knew what we keep forgetting: that a man's wallet is wired directly to his heart, and that how a church handles its money is a spiritual matter from the first peso to the last. So we will not be too pious to talk about money and budgets. We will follow the Master, who looked the subject full in the face and called it by its name — a test.
blocks.es_reference: Hay un viejo mito de que el dinero está de algún modo por debajo del líder espiritual, que un verdadero hombre de Dios no debe ensuciarse las manos con presupuestos y cuentas de banco. Pero usted no puede leer los Evangelios con honradez y creer ese mito. Nuestro Señor habló del dinero constantemente — más de lo que habló del cielo, más de lo que habló de la oración. Él sabía lo que nosotros seguimos olvidando: que la billetera de un hombre está conectada directamente a su corazón, y que cómo maneja una iglesia su dinero es un asunto espiritual desde el primer peso hasta el último. Así que no seremos demasiado piadosos para hablar de pesos y presupuestos. Seguiremos al Maestro, que miró el tema de frente y lo llamó por su nombre — una prueba.

blocks.en: I. You Cannot Serve God and Money
blocks.es_reference: I. No podéis servir a Dios y a las riquezas

blocks.en: Begin where Jesus begins, with a line that allows no middle ground: "No servant can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and mammon" (Luke 16:13). Mammon is money personified, money with a will of its own, money that wants to be lord. And Jesus says you will have a master; the only question is which one. Money is a wonderful servant and a terrible master. Under God it builds churches, feeds the hungry, and sends missionaries. On the throne it corrupts everything it touches, pastors included.
blocks.es_reference: Comience donde Jesús comienza, con una línea que no permite término medio: "Ningún siervo puede servir a dos señores... No podéis servir a Dios y a las riquezas" (Lucas 16:13). Las riquezas (Mamón) son el dinero personificado, el dinero con voluntad propia, el dinero que quiere ser señor. Y Jesús dice que usted tendrá un amo; la única pregunta es cuál. El dinero es un siervo maravilloso y un amo terrible. Bajo Dios construye iglesias, alimenta al hambriento y envía misioneros. En el trono corrompe todo lo que toca, incluidos los pastores.

blocks.en: And just before it, He gives the principle that governs this whole unit: "He who is faithful in what is least is faithful also in much... if you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?" (Luke 16:10-11). Hear what He says. Money is the very least — the training ground. God watches how a man handles the small, the dirty, and the temporary thing of money to decide whether He can trust him with the large and eternal thing of souls. Show me how a pastor handles the offering plate, and I will show you whether God can trust him with a flock. Faithfulness with money is the test that comes before the trust.
blocks.es_reference: Y justo antes, da el principio que gobierna toda esta unidad: "El que es fiel en lo muy poco, también en lo más es fiel... si en las riquezas injustas no fuisteis fieles, ¿quién os confiará lo verdadero?" (Lucas 16:10-11). Oiga lo que dice. El dinero es lo muy poco — el campo de entrenamiento. Dios observa cómo maneja un hombre lo pequeño, lo sucio y lo temporal del dinero para decidir si puede confiarle lo grande y eterno de las almas. Muéstreme cómo maneja un pastor el plato de la ofrenda, y le mostraré si Dios puede confiarle una grey. La fidelidad con las riquezas es la prueba que viene antes de la confianza.

blocks.en: "No servant can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and mammon." — Luke 16:13 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Ningún siervo puede servir a dos señores... No podéis servir a Dios y a las riquezas." — Lucas 16:13 (RVG)

blocks.en: II. The Sacred Trust
blocks.es_reference: II. La confianza sagrada

blocks.en: So whose money is it? Settle it the way we settled the question of the flock in Unit 2: it is not yours. When a widow lays her offering on the plate, she is not paying the pastor; she is giving to God. That money is a sacred trust — the worship of the people, laid on the altar, passing through your hands on its way to the work of God. The man who forgets this and begins to think of the church's money as his money has committed the first and most deadly error of church finance.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces, ¿de quién es el dinero? Resuélvalo como resolvimos la cuestión de la grey en la Unidad 2: no es suyo. Cuando una viuda deja su ofrenda en el plato, no le está pagando al pastor; está dando a Dios. Ese dinero es una confianza sagrada — la adoración del pueblo, puesta sobre el altar, pasando por sus manos camino a la obra de Dios. El hombre que olvida esto y comienza a pensar en el dinero de la iglesia como su dinero ha cometido el primero y más mortal error de las finanzas de la iglesia.

blocks.en: The leader, then, handles the money exactly as he handles the flock: as a steward of what belongs to Another. He will give account for every peso, not first to an auditor but to God. This one conviction — this is God's money, entrusted by His people — will keep a man honest when no one is watching, careful when the amounts are large, and humble when the budget is healthy. Lose that conviction, and no accounting system on earth will save him. Hold it, and he will handle the Lord's money as the holy thing it is.
blocks.es_reference: El líder, pues, maneja el dinero exactamente como maneja la grey: como mayordomo de lo que pertenece a Otro. Dará cuenta de cada peso, no primero a un auditor sino a Dios. Esta sola convicción — este es el dinero de Dios, confiado por su pueblo — mantendrá honrado a un hombre cuando nadie observa, cuidadoso cuando las cantidades son grandes, y humilde cuando el presupuesto está sano. Pierda esa convicción, y ningún sistema contable en la tierra lo salvará. Sosténgala, y manejará el dinero del Señor como la cosa santa que es.

blocks.en: III. Count the Cost: The Budget as a Plan
blocks.es_reference: III. Contad el costo: el presupuesto como plan

blocks.en: Now the practical tool, and notice that Jesus Himself recommends it. "For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost, to see whether he has enough to finish it?" (Luke 14:28). That is budgeting, straight from the lips of the Lord. A church that rushes into commitments without sitting down to count the cost is the man who laid a foundation and could not finish, and "all who see it begin to mock him" (Luke 14:29). Budgeting is not unbelief; it is obedience to a direct word of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora la herramienta práctica, y note que Jesús mismo la recomienda. "Porque ¿quién de vosotros, queriendo edificar una torre, no se sienta primero y cuenta el costo, para ver si tiene lo que necesita para acabarla?" (Lucas 14:28). Eso es presupuestar, directamente de los labios del Señor. Una iglesia que se lanza a compromisos sin sentarse a contar el costo es el hombre que puso un cimiento y no pudo terminar, "y todos los que lo vieren comiencen a hacer burla de él" (Lucas 14:29). Presupuestar no es incredulidad; es obediencia a una palabra directa de Cristo.

blocks.en: So understand what a budget really is. A budget is not a cage; it is a plan expressed in money. It is your priorities translated into numbers. Show me a church budget and I will read you the church's true values, because money does not lie — a church spends on what it truly treasures, whatever it says it treasures. This is why budgeting belongs in a leadership course and not only an accounting course. When you build a budget, you are putting the vision of Unit 3 into figures, deciding before God where the people's offerings will go. Count the cost. Make the plan. Let the money follow the mission.
blocks.es_reference: Así que entienda lo que un presupuesto realmente es. Un presupuesto no es una jaula; es un plan expresado en dinero. Son sus prioridades traducidas a números. Muéstreme un presupuesto de iglesia y le leeré los verdaderos valores de la iglesia, porque el dinero no miente — una iglesia gasta en lo que de veras atesora, diga lo que diga que atesora. Por eso presupuestar pertenece a un curso de liderazgo y no solo a un curso de contabilidad. Cuando construye un presupuesto, está poniendo la visión de la Unidad 3 en cifras, decidiendo delante de Dios a dónde irán las ofrendas del pueblo. Cuente el costo. Haga el plan. Que el dinero siga a la misión.

blocks.en: "For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost...?" — Luke 14:28 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque ¿quién de vosotros, queriendo edificar una torre, no se sienta primero y cuenta el costo...?" — Lucas 14:28 (RVG)

blocks.en: IV. Honest Before All
blocks.es_reference: IV. Honesto delante de todos

blocks.en: Now hear the apostle Paul, who handled an enormous relief offering for Jerusalem, tell you how to keep your hands clean. "Avoiding this: that anyone should blame us in this lavish gift which is administered by us — providing honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men" (2 Corinthians 8:20-21). Read it twice. Paul was an apostle; surely his integrity was beyond question. Yet he refused to carry the money alone. He traveled with trusted brothers chosen by the churches, so that no one could so much as whisper an accusation.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora oiga al apóstol Pablo, que manejó una enorme ofrenda de ayuda para Jerusalén, decirle cómo mantener limpias las manos. "Evitando que nadie nos vitupere en esta abundancia que administramos; procurando hacer las cosas honradamente, no sólo delante del Señor, sino también delante de los hombres" (2 Corintios 8:20-21). Léalo dos veces. Pablo era apóstol; seguramente su integridad estaba fuera de duda. Sin embargo, se negó a llevar el dinero solo. Viajó con hermanos de confianza escogidos por las iglesias, para que nadie pudiera siquiera susurrar una acusación.

blocks.en: There is the rule that has saved a thousand ministries and whose absence has destroyed a thousand more: be honest not only before God, who sees the heart, but before men, who see only the appearance. It is not enough to be honest; you must be visibly honest. This is why a church's money must never be controlled by one person alone — least of all the pastor — by himself. More than one hand counts it. More than one signature releases it. The books are open. There are reports the congregation can see and an audit they can trust. This is not suspicion; it is wisdom and love. The leader who builds these walls of transparency protects the church not only from himself; he protects himself from the accusation that will surely come, and he protects the gospel from reproach. Avoid even the appearance of evil where money is concerned, and you take a weapon out of the enemy's hand.
blocks.es_reference: Ahí está la regla que ha salvado a mil ministerios y cuya ausencia ha destruido a otros mil: sea honesto no solo delante de Dios, que ve el corazón, sino delante de los hombres, que solo ven la apariencia. No basta con ser honesto; debe ser visiblemente honesto. Por eso el dinero de la iglesia nunca debe ser controlado por una sola persona — y menos el pastor — a solas. Más de una mano lo cuenta. Más de una firma lo libera. Los libros están abiertos. Hay informes que la congregación puede ver, y una auditoría en la que pueda confiar. Esto no es sospecha; es sabiduría y amor. El líder que construye estos muros de transparencia no protege a la iglesia solo de sí mismo; se protege a sí mismo de la acusación que ciertamente vendrá, y protege el evangelio del oprobio. Evite aun la apariencia de mal donde el dinero está en juego, y quitará un arma de la mano del enemigo.

blocks.en: "...providing honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men." — 2 Corinthians 8:21 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "...procurando hacer las cosas honradamente, no sólo delante del Señor, sino también delante de los hombres." — 2 Corintios 8:21 (RVG)

blocks.en: V. The Joy of Generosity
blocks.es_reference: V. El gozo de la generosidad

blocks.en: But money in the church is not only to be guarded; it is to be given, and given with joy. "He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. So let each one give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver" (2 Corinthians 9:6-7). And the promise that frees us to give: "And God is able to make all grace abound toward you, that you... may have an abundance for every good work" (2 Corinthians 9:8).
blocks.es_reference: Pero el dinero en la iglesia no solo se ha de guardar; se ha de dar, y dar con gozo. "El que siembra escasamente, también segará escasamente; y el que siembra abundantemente, abundantemente también segará. Cada uno dé como propuso en su corazón; no con tristeza, ni por necesidad; porque Dios ama al dador alegre" (2 Corintios 9:6-7). Y la promesa que nos libera para dar: "Y poderoso es Dios para hacer que abunde en vosotros toda gracia; a fin de que... abundéis para toda buena obra" (2 Corintios 9:8).

blocks.en: A church that speaks of money only to receive it has missed the point entirely. The leader's task is to teach and to model generosity — to lead the people into the sheer joy of cheerful, open-handed giving, because that giving does them good. A generous church is a happy church, and a stingy church is a sick one, however full its accounts. So preach giving not as the church's need to receive but as the giver's privilege to sow, trusting the God who makes grace abound. And let the leaders give first and give most, for no man can call a people to a generosity he does not practice himself.
blocks.es_reference: Una iglesia que solo habla del dinero para recibirlo ha perdido el punto por completo. La tarea del líder es enseñar y modelar la generosidad — guiar al pueblo al puro gozo de un dar alegre y de mano abierta, porque ese dar les hace bien. Una iglesia generosa es una iglesia feliz, y una iglesia tacaña es una iglesia enferma, por llenas que estén sus cuentas. Así que predique el dar no como la necesidad de la iglesia de recibir sino como el privilegio del dador de sembrar, confiando en el Dios que hace abundar la gracia. Y que los líderes den primero y den más, porque ningún hombre puede llamar a un pueblo a una generosidad que él mismo no practica.

blocks.en: VI. The Love of Money
blocks.es_reference: VI. El amor al dinero

blocks.en: Now the warning, sharp and unavoidable. "For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, for which some have strayed from the faith in their greediness, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows" (1 Timothy 6:10). Mark the words well — not money, but the love of money; and not a trivial danger, but a root from which all kinds of evil spring. And note whom Paul warns: not rich pagans, but men who "stray from the faith." Pastors fall here. The overseer, Paul says, must not be "greedy for money" (1 Timothy 3:3).
blocks.es_reference: Ahora la advertencia, aguda e inevitable. "Porque el amor al dinero es la raíz de todos los males; el cual codiciando algunos, se extraviaron de la fe, y fueron traspasados de muchos dolores" (1 Timoteo 6:10). Marque bien las palabras — no el dinero, sino el amor al dinero; no la raíz de un mal, sino la raíz de todos los males. Y note a quién advierte Pablo: no a los paganos ricos, sino a hombres que "se extravían de la fe". Los pastores caen aquí. El obispo, dice Pablo, no ha de ser "codicioso de ganancias deshonestas" (1 Timoteo 3:3).

blocks.en: So the leader must mount a guard over his own heart at exactly the point where money meets ministry. The danger is not that he will steal — most never do. The danger is subtler: that money will quietly rise from servant to master, that he will begin to make decisions for the offering rather than for the Lord, that contentment will slip away and greed move in. The remedy is contentment, "for we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out" (1 Timothy 6:7). Guard your heart, brother. Keep money in its place as a servant, and never let the thing you handle every week become the thing you love.
blocks.es_reference: Así que el líder debe montar guardia sobre su propio corazón justo en el punto donde el dinero se encuentra con el ministerio. El peligro no es que robe — la mayoría nunca lo hace. El peligro es más sutil: que el dinero suba calladamente de siervo a amo, que empiece a tomar decisiones por la ofrenda en vez de por el Señor, que el contentamiento se fugue y la codicia se instale. El remedio es el contentamiento, "porque nada hemos traído a este mundo, y sin duda nada podremos sacar" (1 Timoteo 6:7). Guarde su corazón, hermano. Mantenga el dinero en su lugar como siervo, y nunca deje que aquello que maneja cada semana se vuelva aquello que ama.

blocks.en: "For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil... and pierced themselves through with many sorrows." — 1 Timothy 6:10 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Porque el amor al dinero es la raíz de todos los males... y fueron traspasados de muchos dolores." — 1 Timoteo 6:10 (RVG)

blocks.en: VII. The Laborer Is Worthy
blocks.es_reference: VII. El obrero es digno

blocks.en: Lest all this make us stingy with those who serve, Paul corrects us in the other direction too. "Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and doctrine. For the Scripture says, 'You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain,' and, 'The laborer is worthy of his wages'" (1 Timothy 5:17-18). Faithful stewardship is not only about guarding money from waste; it is about using it justly, and that includes justly providing for those who give their lives to the work.
blocks.es_reference: Para que todo esto no nos vuelva tacaños con quienes sirven, Pablo nos corrige también en la otra dirección. "Los ancianos que gobiernan bien, sean tenidos por dignos de doble honra; mayormente los que trabajan en predicar y enseñar. Pues la Escritura dice: No pondrás bozal al buey que trilla. Y: Digno es el obrero de su salario" (1 Timoteo 5:17-18). La mayordomía fiel no se trata solo de guardar el dinero del despilfarro; se trata de usarlo con justicia, y eso incluye proveer con justicia para quienes dan su vida a la obra.

blocks.en: A church that leaves its pastor and its workers without what they need, while sitting on full accounts, is not being thrifty; it is muzzling the ox, and God notices. So the same budget that funds the mission must also honor the worker. Here is the beautiful balance of this whole unit: the leader himself must not be greedy, but the church must not be stingy with him; he holds money loosely for his own sake, and the church holds him generously for his. Guard it as a steward, give it as a holy thing, and provide for the worker as a just and grateful people. Be faithful with the unrighteous mammon, and the God who tested you with the very least will commit to you the true riches.
blocks.es_reference: Una iglesia que deja a su pastor y a sus obreros sin lo necesario, mientras se sienta sobre cuentas llenas, no está siendo ahorradora; está poniendo bozal al buey, y Dios lo nota. Así que el mismo presupuesto que financia la misión también debe honrar al obrero. Aquí está el hermoso equilibrio de toda esta unidad: el líder mismo no debe ser avaricioso, pero la iglesia no debe ser tacaña con él; él sostiene el dinero con holgura por su propio bien, y la iglesia lo sostiene con generosidad por el bien de él. Guárdelo como mayordomo, délo como santo, y provea para el obrero como un pueblo justo y agradecido. Sea fiel con las riquezas injustas, y el Dios que lo probó con lo muy poco le confiará las verdaderas riquezas.

blocks.en: "The laborer is worthy of his wages." — 1 Timothy 5:18 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Digno es el obrero de su salario." — 1 Timoteo 5:18 (RVG)

mc.stem: How often did Jesus speak about money, according to this unit?
options: More than He spoke of heaven or prayer
mc.why: Jesus spoke of money constantly — more than of heaven or prayer — because the wallet is wired to the heart.

mc.stem: 'You cannot serve God and mammon' teaches that money is:
options: A wonderful servant but a terrible master
mc.why: Money is a wonderful servant and a terrible master; you will have a master — the question is which.

mc.stem: In Luke 16:10-11, money is described as the 'least' because it is:
options: The training ground God uses before trusting a man with souls
mc.why: Money is the training ground; God watches how a man handles it before trusting him with souls.

mc.stem: Whose money is the church's offering, according to the unit?
options: God's, a sacred trust given by His people
mc.why: The offering is given to God; it is a sacred trust passing through the leader's hands to God's work.

mc.stem: The first and most deadly error of church finance is:
options: Thinking of the church's money as one's own
mc.why: Forgetting the money is God's and treating it as one's own is the first and deadliest error.

mc.stem: According to Luke 14:28, a budget is essentially:
options: Counting the cost — a plan Jesus Himself recommends
mc.why: Jesus told builders to count the cost first; budgeting is obedience to a direct word of Christ.

mc.stem: A church budget, rightly understood, is:
options: A secret kept from the people
A plan expressed in money — priorities translated into numbers
mc.why: A budget is not a cage but a plan in money form; it reveals a church's true values.

mc.stem: Why does the unit say 'money does not lie'?
options: A church spends on what it truly treasures
mc.why: A budget reveals real values because a church spends on what it truly treasures, whatever it claims.

mc.stem: Why did Paul refuse to carry the Jerusalem relief offering alone?
options: So no one could even whisper an accusation
mc.why: Though his integrity was beyond question, Paul traveled with trusted brothers to prevent any accusation.

mc.stem: 'Honorable... not only before the Lord but before men' means a leader must be:
options: Not merely honest but visibly honest
mc.why: It is not enough to be honest before God; one must be visibly honest before men as well.

mc.stem: Which practice does the unit require for handling church money?
options: More than one hand counts it and more than one signature releases it
mc.why: Money must never be controlled by one person alone; multiple hands count and multiple signatures release it.

mc.stem: Transparency in church finances is described as:
options: Wisdom and love that also protect the leader and the gospel
mc.why: Transparency is wisdom and love; it protects the church, the leader from accusation, and the gospel from reproach.

mc.stem: According to 2 Corinthians 9:7, God loves:
options: The one who gives by necessity
mc.why: Each should give as he purposes in his heart, not grudgingly; for God loves a cheerful giver.

mc.stem: How should a leader preach giving?
options: As the church's need to receive
As the giver's privilege to sow, trusting God who makes grace abound
mc.why: Preach giving as the giver's joyful privilege to sow, not as the church's need to receive.

mc.stem: First Timothy 6:10 warns that the root of all kinds of evil is:
mc.why: Not money but the LOVE of money is the root; some have strayed from the faith through greed.

mc.stem: The subtle danger of money for a pastor is usually that:
options: He will give too much away
Money quietly rises from servant to master in his heart
mc.why: Most pastors never steal; the subtler danger is money rising from servant to master and greed moving in.

mc.stem: The remedy the unit prescribes against the love of money is:
options: Contentment ('we brought nothing into this world')
mc.why: The remedy is contentment, remembering we brought nothing in and can carry nothing out (1 Tim 6:7).

mc.stem: First Timothy 5:17-18 ('do not muzzle the ox') teaches that the church must:
options: Justly provide for those who labor in the work
mc.why: Faithful stewardship includes justly providing for those who labor; a church that withholds muzzles the ox.

mc.stem: The 'beautiful balance' of this unit is that:
options: The leader must not be greedy, yet the church must not be stingy with him
Both leader and church should be frugal to the bone
The leader hoards and the church spends
mc.why: He holds money loosely for his own sake; the church holds him generously for his — a beautiful balance.

mc.stem: The governing principle of Unit 5 is that faithfulness with money:
options: Is the test that comes before God entrusts the true riches of souls
mc.why: Be faithful with the least (money) and God will commit to you the true riches; it is the test before the trust.

sa.prompt: Why is how a church handles money a spiritual matter, and how did Jesus treat the subject?
sa.model: How a church handles money is a spiritual matter because a man's wallet is wired directly to his heart; Jesus said you cannot serve God and money, so money is never neutral but reveals whom you treasure. Far from treating it as beneath the spiritual leader, Jesus spoke about money constantly, more than He spoke of heaven or prayer, and He called it a test: he who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much. Money is a wonderful servant and a terrible master, and God watches how a man handles it to decide whether He can trust him with the eternal riches of souls.

sa.prompt: Explain why the church's money is a 'sacred trust' and how that conviction guards a leader.
sa.model: The church's money is a sacred trust because when a member gives, she is not paying the pastor but giving to God; the offering is the people's worship, laid on the altar and passing through the leader's hands to God's work. It belongs to Another, so the leader handles it as a steward who will give account for every peso, first to God and not merely to an auditor. This one conviction — that it is God's money, entrusted by His people — keeps a man honest when no one watches, careful when amounts are large, and humble when the budget is healthy. Lose the conviction and no accounting system can save him; hold it and he treats the money as the holy thing it is.

sa.prompt: How does Luke 14:28 make budgeting an act of obedience, and what is a budget really?
sa.model: In Luke 14:28 Jesus says a wise builder sits down first and counts the cost to see whether he can finish, so budgeting is not unbelief but obedience to a direct word of Christ; a church that rushes into commitments without counting the cost is the builder who could not finish and is mocked. A budget is not a cage but a plan expressed in money — the church's priorities translated into numbers. Money does not lie, so a budget reveals a church's true values, since a church spends on what it truly treasures. That is why budgeting belongs to leadership: building a budget puts the vision into figures and decides before God where the people's offerings will go, letting the money follow the mission.

sa.prompt: What does Paul's example in 2 Corinthians 8:20-21 teach about financial transparency?
sa.model: Paul handled a large relief offering and, though his integrity was beyond question, refused to carry the money alone; he traveled with trusted brothers chosen by the churches so that no one could even whisper an accusation. This teaches that a leader must be honest not only before God, who sees the heart, but before men, who see only the appearance — it is not enough to be honest, one must be visibly honest. So church money should never be controlled by one person alone, least of all the pastor: more than one hand counts it, more than one signature releases it, the books are open, and there are reports and an audit the people can trust. This transparency is not suspicion but wisdom and love, protecting the church, the leader, and the gospel.

sa.prompt: How should a leader teach generosity, and why is a generous church a healthy one?
sa.model: A leader should teach and model generosity, leading the people into the sheer joy of cheerful, open-handed giving, because God loves a cheerful giver and such giving does the giver good. He should preach giving not as the church's need to receive but as the giver's privilege to sow, trusting the God who makes all grace abound so the people have enough for every good work. A generous church is a healthy, happy church, while a stingy church is a sick one however full its accounts, because the heart that gives freely is right with God. And the leaders must give first and give most, for no one can call a people to a generosity he does not practice himself.

sa.prompt: Explain 1 Timothy 6:10 carefully: what exactly is the danger, and whom does Paul warn?
sa.model: First Timothy 6:10 says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, and the words must be marked carefully: not money itself but the love of it, and not a trivial danger but a root from which all kinds of evil spring. Paul warns not rich pagans but men who stray from the faith in their greed and pierce themselves with many sorrows — and pastors fall here, which is why the overseer must not be greedy for money. The danger is rarely outright theft; it is subtler, that money quietly rises from servant to master, that a leader begins deciding for the offering rather than for the Lord, and that contentment slips away while greed moves in. So the leader must guard his heart where money meets ministry.

sa.prompt: What does 'do not muzzle the ox' (1 Timothy 5:17-18) require of a church?
sa.model: 'Do not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain' requires a church to provide justly for those who labor in the work, for the laborer is worthy of his wages and the elders who rule well, especially those who labor in word and doctrine, are worthy of double honor. Faithful stewardship is not only guarding money from waste but using it justly, and that includes fair provision for the pastor and workers. A church that leaves its workers without what they need while sitting on full accounts is not thrifty but is muzzling the ox, and God notices. So the same budget that funds the mission must also honor the worker, providing for him as a just and grateful people.

sa.prompt: Describe the 'beautiful balance' Unit 5 strikes between the leader and the church regarding money.
sa.model: The beautiful balance is that the leader himself must not be greedy, holding money loosely as a servant for his own spiritual good, while the church must not be stingy with him, holding him generously for his good. These two truths protect each other: a leader guarding his heart against the love of money does not grasp for more, and a church obeying the command not to muzzle the ox provides fairly for its workers. So the same unit that warns the leader against greed also warns the church against tightfistedness. He keeps money in its place as a servant, and the church provides justly for those who labor, so that the money guards no one's idol yet leaves no faithful worker in need.

sa.prompt: Connect the principle of Luke 16:10 to the leader's broader ministry of souls.
sa.model: Luke 16:10 says he who is faithful in the least is faithful also in much, and that if a man is not faithful with unrighteous mammon, no one will commit to him the true riches. Money is the least — the small, temporary training ground — while souls are the true and eternal riches. God uses a leader's handling of money to test whether He can trust him with people, so the offering plate is a proving ground for the pastorate itself. A man careless or dishonest with money reveals he cannot yet be trusted with souls, while one faithful in finances shows the character God will entrust with His flock. So faithfulness with money is never separate from the ministry of souls; it is the test that comes before the trust.

sa.prompt: Summarize Unit 5: how should a faithful leader handle the church's money from first peso to last?
sa.model: Unit 5 teaches that a faithful leader handles the church's money as a sacred trust from first peso to last. He remembers it is God's money, given by His people, and so manages it as a steward who will give account. He budgets, counting the cost as Jesus commanded, letting a plan in money form follow the mission and reveal true values. He builds transparency so he is honest not only before God but visibly before men, never controlling money alone. He teaches and models cheerful generosity rather than mere fundraising. He guards his own heart against the love of money, the root of all kinds of evil, with contentment. And he ensures the church justly provides for its workers, not muzzling the ox. Faithful in the least, he is entrusted by God with the true riches of souls.
